summary: Both tables report institution-level activity during the 12-month period from July 1, 2012, through June 30, 2013, for undergraduate and graduate levels. The supplied descriptions specify no additional sector, degree-granting, admissions, or other eligibility restriction; the records summarize institutional activity rather than individual students.

The Completions survey is collected annually in the winter and reports awards, students receiving awards, and related program offerings for activity from July 1, 2012, through June 30, 2013. The unit of observation is the reporting postsecondary institution, with aggregate records rather than individual students; eligible and required IPEDS institutions report their applicable completions and programs. Coverage therefore reflects institutional reporting and applies to institutions in the IPEDS postsecondary universe that offer reportable certificates, degrees, or programs.

Fall Enrollment covers IPEDS postsecondary institutions reporting fall enrollment. Traditional academic-year institutions report enrollment as of October 15 or their official fall reporting date; institutions with program-specific or continuous calendars report students enrolled at any time from August 1 through October 31. The unit is the institution identified by UNITID, with multiple records when a table breaks enrollment into student characteristics or levels.

This annual Finance survey collects institution-level financial data for fiscal year 2013 during the winter 2013–14 IPEDS collection cycle. Reporting is mandatory for eligible postsecondary institutions participating in Title IV, with data reported for the institution as a whole rather than by student or program. The survey covers institutional revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities, and institutions report on the accounting-standard form appropriate to their sector and accounting model.

The Graduation Rates survey reports outcomes as of August 31, 2013 for cohorts of full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students at eligible four-year, two-year, and less-than-two-year institutions. Its unit is an institution-level cohort outcome record, covering enrollment, completion within specified percentages of normal time, and—in applicable tables—transfer-out status. Cohorts and completion windows vary by institution level and table, so the relevant table depends on the institution sector and the requested follow-up period.

Human Resources reports institutional staff on the payroll as of November 1 for fall collections and salary information for the academic year. Records are organized by institution, with multiple records per institution for applicable staff categories, and coverage is limited to institutions eligible for the relevant IPEDS Human Resources component; some tables further restrict coverage to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices. Human Resources reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so the 2013 odd-numbered collection has data under the catalog’s reporting rule.

These institution-level Institutional Characteristics data cover the 2013-14 academic year and were collected in the fall 2013 reporting window. The universe is the institutions in the 2013-14 IPEDS universe; Title IV institutions participating in federal financial aid programs are required to report, while applicability varies by component and institution. Some fields are conditional on characteristics such as open-admission status, academic calendar, program type, or reporting relationship, and response-status data identify nonresponse, imputation, and component applicability.

The Student Financial Aid survey covers the July 1, 2012–June 30, 2013 academic year and is reported only in odd-numbered years, so 2013 has data. The unit of observation is the institution, with measures for undergraduate students at institutions in the IPEDS universe that are eligible to report student financial aid data. The survey covers both full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates and, for selected measures, all undergraduates.
